schemes.official_name: King's Business School Consultancy (Strategy consultancy support for London enterprises; originally Business Consultancy Scheme)
schemes.description: King's Business School offers up to 15 enterprises in its local boroughs free consultancy. Each enterprise gets a team of 3-4 final-year undergraduate consultants from economics, business and/or management degrees. Topics include HR planning, marketing and social media, financial analysis, strategy and data analysis. Teams finish by delivering a final analysis and recommendations as a presentation and written report to the client. Projects are supervised by the Vice Dean Education. The scheme started as a pilot with Westminster City Council: 18 final-year students from BSc Business Management and BSc Economics & Management were selected and split into five groups.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Final-year undergraduates on economics, business and/or management degrees (pilot: BSc Business Management, BSc Economics & Management)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Final-year KBS economics/business/management undergraduates; pilot students were selected
schemes.duration: Programme length not stated; a 'summer 2026 programme' is advertised, and one result also mentions a closing week of w/c 30 November
schemes.delivery_format: Consultancy teams working with local enterprises; presentation + written report
schemes.project_evidence: Defined consultancy brief for an enterprise, ending in final analysis and recommendations as a presentation and written report [1].
schemes.group_evidence: 'a student consultancy team of three to four students' per enterprise [1]; pilot students split into five groups [2].
schemes.employer_evidence: Local enterprises are the clients: they receive free consultancy, and the presentation and written report are delivered to them; students may sign NDAs at the client's request [1].
schemes.partner_role: Client enterprise sets the business issue and receives the recommendations; the pilot was run in partnership with Westminster City Council (public sector)
schemes.named_partners: Westminster City Council (pilot partner; year not shown in extract)
schemes.deliverable: Client presentation + written report of recommendations
schemes.participation_data: Up to 15 enterprises per round (capacity, page undated); pilot: 18 students in 5 groups (year not shown)
schemes.unresolved: Whether the scheme carries credit; exact timing (the summer 2026 call conflicts with the 'w/c 30 November' close); how students are selected now. Current status rests on the page saying applications for the summer 2026 programme are open.

profile_md:
**King's College London** (partial review) has live-client project provision spread across the Business School, Informatics and central civic and careers units. Some routes are confirmed to involve group working; for others it is unverified.

- **Fully qualifying, current:** The **King's Business School Consultancy** places teams of 3-4 final-year economics, business and management undergraduates with up to 15 local enterprises. Teams deliver a presentation and written recommendations, and a summer 2026 call is open.
- **Qualifying but undated:** On the **MSc Advanced Software Engineering**, teams build software for external partners, including public-sector challenges with AWS mentors (Richmond and Wandsworth Councils). The **Careers Insights Programme** runs 2-week group virtual micro-internships on employer-proposed briefs for final-year undergraduates across all nine faculties.
- **Live clients, group working unclear:** Informatics' **Knowledge Exchange Projects** (over 90 since 2022; partners set the brief, join supervision and receive the software; up to five students per brief; 2025/26 confirmed). **PPM Consultancy** (NHS trusts, Hackney, charities; Jan-Apr 2026). The MSc International Management **Business Consulting Project** (competitive, 45 credits).
- **Civic routes:** The **Civic Leadership Academy** (charity partners; 2025-26 Kickstarter challenge with student groups and a 6-week project internship) and the **King's Civic Challenge** (student-staff-charity teams pitching for up to £5,000; no current round found).
- **No external client evidenced:** Team projects without an evidenced external client include the second-year Software Engineering Group Project and the Engineering MEng group project.
